newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Bank of Queensland wants independence.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Bank of Queensland wants independence.

text.p: Bank of Queensland Ltd chairman Neil Roberts said on Friday that he would do "whatever is necessary" to prevent a strategic 44 percent of the bank being acquired by the state government's new bank consortium.
Roberts said the bank still rejected a government offer to join in the merger of the government-owned Suncorp, Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) and Metway Bank Ltd.
"We will do whatever is necessary to stop our shares going across to (Metway), one of our major competitors," Roberts said.

Roberts told Reuters he was convinced Suncorp's 44 percent stake in the bank would be absorbed as part of the bank merger plan, despite amendments to legislation this week that prevented the transfer of that stake unless a majority of shareholders agreed. Roberts said the 44 percent stake was held by Suncorp under an exemption granted by the federal treasurer.
Under the Banks (Shareholdings) Act, a holding of more than 15 percent was not permitted "unless the treasurer is positively satisfied it is in the national interest," Roberts said.

Roberts said a Bank of Queensland proposal to buy back 30 percent of the 44 percent stake was made to the state government several weeks ago. "I think a commercial solution is possible and I hope we will be able to solve this," he said.
There were still several other options available to the bank - "we've got a programme worked out," he said.
The Bank of Queensland was invited in May to join the government's merger proposal but it rejected the government offer of A$4.70 a share plus a special 75 cent dividend.
